item.title: Ethan Salas’ first 2 MLB homers power Padres past Rockies
item.description: Ethan Salas hit the first two home runs of his major league career, Jackson Merrill finished with three hits and the San Diego Padres beat the Colorado Rockies 9-3 in Denver on Wednesday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Ethan Salas hit the first two home runs of his major league career, Jackson Merrill finished with three hits and the San Diego Padres beat the Colorado Rockies 9-3 in Denver on Wednesday night. Samad Taylor, Jake Cronenworth and Dustin Harris had two hits each and Robbie Ray tossed six solid innings to help the Padres win for the ninth time in the last 10 games. San Diego (83-69) retained the third National League wild-card spot, one game behind the Philadelphia Phillies and 1 1/2 games back of the Chicago Cubs, who hold the top spot in the wild-card standings. Salas, playing in his ninth game since making his major league debut on Sept. 2, drove in three runs. At 20 years, 107 days old, he is the youngest catcher in MLB history with a multi-homer game, according to MLB.com. Kyle Karros homered for Colorado (56-96), which has lost nine of its last 10. The Padres took a 2-0 lead in the first inning on a sacrifice fly followed by Cronenworth's RBI single. The Rockies answered with a run in the bottom of the frame on a bases-loaded groundout by Adael Amador. Salas made it 3-1 when he led off the second inning with his first homer of the night, Harris hit a triple to right in the fourth to tack on another run and San Diego broke it open in the fifth. Merrill started the rally with a one-out single, and Xander Bogaerts drew a walk that ended Adams' night. After a groundout moved the runners up, Taylor drove them in with a single and Salas followed with a two-run homer off Nick Frasso to make it 8-1. Adams (0-1) allowed six runs on eight hits over 4 1/3 innings. Ty France's RBI double in the sixth extended the lead for Ray (13-8), who allowed just one hit through the first five innings. He gave up a two-run homer to Karros in the sixth, Karros' 12th home run of the season, but got the next two to end his night. He allowed three runs on three hits and fanned six over six innings. --Field Level Media

item.title: WTA roundup: Marta Kostyuk gets walkover vs. Taylor Townsend (illness)
item.description: Top-seeded Marta Kostyuk is through to the quarterfinals of the Guadalajara Open even though she has yet to play a point in the Mexican tournament.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Top-seeded Marta Kostyuk is through to the quarterfinals of the Guadalajara Open even though she has yet to play a point in the Mexican tournament. The Ukrainian received a first-round bye, and she got a walkover in her scheduled second-round match on Wednesday when Taylor Townsend withdrew due to an illness. Townsend and partner Katerina Siniakova of the Czech Republic achieved a career Grand Slam when they won the U.S. Open women's doubles title on Friday in New York. The pair captured the Wimbledon title in 2024, the Australian Open in 2025, and the French Open earlier this year. Kostyuk is now scheduled to get her tournament underway against eighth-seeded Liudmila Samsonova of Russia, who edged Kayla Day 7-6 (4), 2-6, 7-6 (5) in the last match Wednesday night. In the day's other second-round action, second-seeded Iva Jovic, the defending champion, topped Turkey's Zeynep Sonmez 7-6 (5), 6-4, and seventh-seeded Magdalena Frech eliminated Caroline Dolehide 6-4, 6-3. SP Open Serbia's Teodora Kostovic became the first player to reach the quarterfinals at Sao Paulo, ousting ninth-seeded Darja Semenistaja of Latvia 6-4, 6-1. Kostovic, 19, will compete in a WTA Tour-level quarterfinal for the first time after saving five of the six break points she faced. The rest of the day's action consisted of the remainder of the rain-delayed first round. Winners included second-seeded Paula Badosa of Spain, third-seeded Solana Sierra of Argentina, fourth-seeded Anna Blinkova of Russia, fifth-seeded Eva Lys of Germany, seventh-seeded Kaitlin Quevedo of Spain and eighth-seeded Alina Charaeva of Armenia. The Czech Republic's Dominika Salkova downed sixth-seeded Jessica Bouzas Maneiro of Spain 7-5, 6-1. --Field Level Media

item.title: Rangers rally past Red Sox, forge first-place tie in AL West
item.description: The Texas Rangers broke open a tie game by scoring three runs in the seventh inning and defeated the visiting Boston Red Sox 7-3 on Wednesday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Texas Rangers broke open a tie game by scoring three runs in the seventh inning and defeated the visiting Boston Red Sox 7-3 on Wednesday night. Texas' seventh featured Brandon Nimmo's RBI double that drove in Corey Seager to give the Rangers (76-76) a 4-3 lead, and Ezequiel Duran's two-run single that scored Jake Burger and Nimmo to push the lead to 6-3. All three runs were charged to reliever Erik Miller (4-1). Nate Eovaldi (11-9) pitched four scoreless innings in relief to earn the win, holding Boston to one hit. The win moved Texas into a tie with Houston for first place in the American League West, although the Astros own the tiebreaker. Willson Contreras homered for the Red Sox, who were limited to three hits and will try to salvage the three-game series finale Thursday. Boston (82-70) holds a five-game lead over the Chicago White Sox for the second AL wild-card spot. Contreras hit a two-run homer, his team-high 27th, against Texas starter MacKenzie Gore to put Boston up 2-0 in the top of the first. Gore pitched four-plus innings and gave up three runs on two hits. Josh Jung had three of the Rangers' 13 hits. Burger and Justin Foscue each added two hits. One of Burger's hits was a ground-rule double that drove in Foscue and cut Boston's lead to 2-1 in the bottom of the first against starter Jake Bennett. Texas tied the game on Foscue's RBI single that scored Wyatt Langford in the fourth, but Boston took a 3-2 lead in the fifth when Caleb Durbin scored on a Jakob Junis balk. The Rangers pulled even again in the fifth. Jung hit a leadoff double and scored on Langford's two-out single off reliever Greg Weissert to make it 3-3. Bennett allowed three runs on eight hits in 4 2/3 innings, striking out seven and walking one. Texas took control in the seventh and extended the lead to 7-3 in the eighth on Seager's RBI single. --Field Level Media

item.title: Astros stumble against Royals, fall into tie for first in AL West
item.description: John Rave and Michael Massey smacked home runs in support of left-hander Daniel Lynch IV, who twirled five shutout innings to lead the visiting Kansas City Royals to a 5-2 victory over the Houston Astros on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: John Rave and Michael Massey smacked home runs in support of left-hander Daniel Lynch IV, who twirled five shutout innings to lead the visiting Kansas City Royals to a 5-2 victory over the Houston Astros on Wednesday. The Royals (67-85) squared the three-game series and set up a decisive game on Thursday. The Astros (76-76) dropped into a tie atop the American League West with the Texas Rangers (76-76), who beat the Boston Red Sox 7-3. Massey, who ended up 3-for-5, led off the fourth inning with a bloop single. Rave followed two batters later with his sixth home run, snapping a scoreless tie. Rave drilled a 2-2 cutter from Astros starter Cristian Javier 366 feet to right field. Javier (2-6) departed with one out in the sixth with two runners on base. Astros reliever Bryan King cleaned up that mess, and Javier capped his ledger with two runs allowed on five hits and three walks. He struck out two. The Royals' three-run eighth inning padded the lead to 5-0. Massey led off that frame with his 12th home run, clanking the first pitch from Astros reliever Enyel De Los Santos off the right field foul pole. Josh Rojas and Isaac Collins walked with two outs before Carter Jensen followed with a double to right, plating Rojas. Collins also scored on the play due to right fielder Jorge Barrosa's throwing error. Lynch (6-5) cruised through his eighth start since joining the rotation last month. He retired seven consecutive batters following Jeremy Pena's leadoff double in the first, and he retired the final seven batters he faced, starting with Yordan Alvarez's inning-ending double play in the third. Lynch permitted two hits and a walk while fanning three. Royals reliever Anthony Gose preserved the two-run lead in the seventh by retiring pinch hitter Nelson Velazquez and Daulton Varsho with two runners on base. Houston got on the scoreboard thanks to Isaac Paredes' eighth-inning sacrifice fly. Yainer Diaz homered off Royals reliever Steven Cruz leading off the ninth, his 12th of the year. --Field Level Media

item.title: Chelsea's Joao Pedro out of Brazil's friendlies against Australia, India with injury
item.description: Chelsea striker Joao Pedro has withdrawn from Brazil's friendlies against Australia and India due to injury, the national team said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chelsea striker Joao Pedro has withdrawn from Brazil's friendlies against Australia and India due to injury, the national team said on Wednesday. The 24-year-old played the full game for [USN:L1N45404K TEXT:"Chelsea in a 2-2"] draw with Hull City in the Premier League on Saturday, scoring one goal and setting up another. Brazil did not specify the nature of Joao Pedro's injury but said in a social media post that Fluminense midfielder Matheus Martinelli had been called up as his replacement. Brazil will visit Australia for two friendlies on September 25 and September 29, before playing India in Kolkata on October 3.

item.title: Pete Crow-Armstrong homers twice to carry Cubs past Braves
item.description: Pete Crow-Armstrong homered twice and Shota Imanaga threw six quality innings to help lead the Chicago Cubs to an 8-4 victory over the visiting Atlanta Braves on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Pete Crow-Armstrong homered twice and Shota Imanaga threw six quality innings to help lead the Chicago Cubs to an 8-4 victory over the visiting Atlanta Braves on Wednesday. Crow-Armstrong hit solo homers in the third and seventh to bring his season total to 44 -- one behind Philadelphia's Kyle Schwarber's major league-leading 45. Alex Bregman went 3-for-4 with a homer and four RBIs for the Cubs (85-68), who kept pace a half-game ahead of the Phillies for the National League's top wild card spot. Imanaga (11-10) won his third consecutive start for the first time this season. The left-hander allowed just one run on four hits while striking out eight and walking none. J.R. Ritchie (1-3) allowed six runs on seven hits across 4 2/3 innings for Atlanta (89-64). The rookie struck out five and walked two in his first major league appearance since Aug. 2. Mauricio Dubon had two hits and an RBI for the Braves, who have dropped three of their last four. Michael Busch walked and scored in the first on Bregman's double. Crow-Armstrong doubled the Cubs' lead with his 43rd homer of the season -- a 376-foot solo shot in the third. Chicago tacked on in the fourth with Bregman's 26th home run, extending the lead to 3-0. After Austin Riley reached on an infield single in the second, Imanaga retired 11 straight Atlanta batters. In the fifth, Carson Kelly singled and Crow-Armstrong tripled to make it 4-0. After Ritchie hit Seiya Suzuki with a pitch and struck out Busch, Bregman lined a ball past Riley at third base. Both Crow-Armstrong and Suzuki scored as Dubon misplayed the ball in right, resulting in a triple for Bregman. Ronald Acuna Jr. began the sixth with a double before advancing to third on Drake Baldwin's groundout. Matt Olson then plated the first Atlanta run with a grounder to first. Aaron Civale relieved Imanaga in the seventh. He allowed Dubon's triple and Riley's RBI groundout. Owen Murphy served up Crow-Armstrong's second blast to begin the bottom of the seventh. In the eighth, Tyrone Taylor doubled and scored on Michael Conforto's single to make it 8-2. Ryan Rolison surrendered Ozzie Albies' walk and Michael Harris II's single in the ninth before Ryan Zeferjahn entered in relief. Dubon then drove in the Braves' third run with a double to right. Sean Murphy followed two batters later with an RBI groundout. Zeferjahn retired Mike Yastrzemski to end the game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jets suspend G Connor Hellebuyck for failing to report to camp
item.description: Winnipeg goaltender Connor Hellebuyck, who publicly requested a trade last month, was suspended by the team Wednesday after failing to report to training camp.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Winnipeg goaltender Connor Hellebuyck, who publicly requested a trade last month, was suspended by the team Wednesday after failing to report to training camp. The 33-year-old veteran has spent all 11 of his NHL seasons with the Jets, winning the Vezina Trophy as the league's top goalie three times and capturing the Hart Trophy as the NHL's most valuable player in 2024-25. The average annual value of Hellebuyck's seven-year contract, signed in October 2023, is $8.5 million. Hellebuyck issued a statement through agent Ray Petkau that read, "I have tried to handle the situation quietly and respectfully while giving the organization time to explore its options. With training camp approaching, I felt it was important to publicly confirm my (trade) request. My position has not changed. I believe moving on is the best path forward for me and my family." Winnipeg general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff will hold a press conference Thursday. No details about the terms or length of the suspension were announced. According to multiple media reports, the Jets previously held trade talks with the Buffalo Sabres regarding Hellebuyck. The Utah Mammoth, Carolina Hurricanes and New Jersey Devils also reportedly have interest. Hellebuyck had a down season by his standards in 2025-26, finishing 23-23-11 with a 2.86 goals-against average and a career-worst .895 save percentage. Winnipeg failed to make the playoffs, going 35-35-12. The prior season, en route to the Hart and Vezina honors, he went 47-12-3 with a .925 save percentage and league-best figures in GAA (2.00) and shutouts (eight). Overall in 625 NHL games, Hellebuyck has a 345-208-55 record with a 2.58 GAA and a .916 save percentage. He also led Team USA to the gold medal at the 2026 Milano Cortina Olympics. The Jets open the preseason against the host Edmonton Oilers on Saturday, and they start the regular season at home against the Boston Bruins on Oct. 2. --Field Level Media

item.title: LSU QB Sam Leavitt (undisclosed) doubtful vs. Ole Miss
item.description: Though he did not appear to suffer an injury in last Saturday's win over Louisiana Tech, quarterback Sam Leavitt is listed as doubtful for No. 7 LSU's rivalry showdown at No. 8 Ole Miss on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Though he did not appear to suffer an injury in last Saturday's win over Louisiana Tech, quarterback Sam Leavitt is listed as doubtful for No. 7 LSU's rivalry showdown at No. 8 Ole Miss on Saturday. According to On3, Leavitt is dealing with a sore throwing shoulder and has been limited in practice this week. The Tigers are closely monitoring their starting quarterback, per the report. The Arizona State transfer spoke to reporters after the 45-14 home victory and did not appear to be dealing with an ailment. "I'm just focusing on tonight, getting better, getting the body healthy," Leavitt said when asked whether he was looking forward to facing Ole Miss. "But no, it's going to be an incredible opportunity." Leavitt was slated to speak with the media Tuesday about the key SEC clash against Ole Miss, according to an LSU spokesperson, but he was not present at the session. At a Monday news conference, LSU coach Lane Kiffin did not mention any information about Leavitt's health status. Under the SEC's availability policy, a player has a 25% chance to play and is "unlikely to play due to significant concerns." SEC football teams face penalties that range from $25,000 to $100,000 for late or inaccurate availability reports. It is at the discretion of SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey whether to impose these penalties. Leavitt's teammate and the Tigers' leading tackler, TJ Dottery, is also questionable. A two-year starter and Big 12 Freshman of the Year at Arizona State, Leavitt transferred to LSU after the school hired Kiffin. After throwing for a touchdown and rushing for two more in a blowout season-opening win over Clemson, Leavitt threw for a score and ran for three more in the victory over Louisiana Tech, but he tossed three interceptions. In two games with LSU, Leavitt has completed 41 of 66 passes for 574 yards, two touchdowns and four interceptions. He has also rushed for 135 yards and five scores. If Leavitt isn't available to play, either freshman Husan Longstreet or sophomore Landen Clark will start. In two games, Clark has completed 7 of 10 passes for 109 yards, one touchdown, and no interceptions. Longstreet has attempted one pass, a 33-yard completion. --Field Level Media

item.title: Hawkish Fed adds to rupee's troubles, traders watch 96/USD hurdle
item.description: The Indian rupee is expected to be under pressure on Thursday and could weaken past the 96-per-dollar handle after the U.S. Federal Reserve raised interest rates and signalled that further tightening is in the pipeline.
item.dc:creator: Jaspreet Kalra
item.content:encoded: The Indian rupee is expected to be under pressure on Thursday and could weaken past the 96-per-dollar handle after the U.S. Federal Reserve raised interest rates and signalled that further tightening is in the pipeline. The rupee is expected to open slightly weaker around 96-96.05 per dollar, down from its previous close of 95.9550. The Fed [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"raised interest rates"] by 25 basis points on Wednesday, its first increase since 2023, with officials expecting one more increase this year. The hike pushed the dollar index above the 100 mark to its highest level in more than a month. Asian currencies slipped on Thursday, while equities traded mixed as investors digested the prospect of higher global borrowing costs. The Fed's hike follows a rate increase in Europe last week and precedes an anticipated rise in Japan on Friday, as central banks globally grapple with rising inflation. "There are no immediate signs for inflation to ease, especially given the stalemate in the Middle East. This means the Fed may need to continue to tighten in order to achieve its target," Tai Hui, APAC chief market strategist at J.P. Morgan Asset Management, said in a note. Futures imply about a 50% chance of another Fed hike next month to rein in inflation. A total of three rate increases have been priced in for this tightening cycle. The rate outlook is expected to add to pressure on the rupee, already weighed down by elevated oil prices and foreign portfolio outflows from Indian stocks and bonds. Traders said that inflows linked to the IPO of India's largest stock exchange, along with interventions by the Reserve Bank of India, could help cushion the rupee. However, sentiment may worsen if the currency weakens past 96 and remains there, they added. The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) will open for subscriptions on Thursday after [USN:L4N4580ZT TEXT:"allocating"] shares worth $703 million to anchor investors on Wednesday.

item.title: Peter Max, known for groovy art that came to symbolize the 60s, dies at 88
item.description: Pop artist Peter Max, whose dreamy, boldly colored works provided an artistic backdrop for the 1960s U.S. hippie movement and made him a commercial art powerhouse, died on Monday at a hospital in Manhattan at the age of 88, a spokesperson for his family said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pop artist Peter Max, whose dreamy, boldly colored works provided an artistic backdrop for the 1960s U.S. hippie movement and made him a commercial art powerhouse, died on Monday at a hospital in Manhattan at the age of 88, a spokesperson for his family said on Wednesday. Max's visions – often influenced by his love of astronomy – were everywhere in the '60s and '70s and almost as much a part of the decade's youth culture as sex, drugs and rock 'n' roll. They were like artistic renderings of an acid trip and were, in the vernacular of the time, really groovy. The colors were vibrant and the images surreal - cosmic landscapes and starbursts, doves and floating peace symbols, kaleidoscopic butterflies, puffy clouds and other flower-power imagery. Rock stars such as the Beatles, Jimi Hendrix and Mick Jagger were Max's portrait subjects, as well as his friends. President Ronald Reagan was a fan and Max donated a painting of the Statue of Liberty to the Reagan Presidential Library. "His decorative posters show Max to be a visionary fascinated by time, space and evolution," a 1967 Village Voice critique said. "A psychedelic skyline prophesizes the day when skyscrapers may be temples, when the Rockefeller Center's Rainbow Room may be used for meditation." Max is survived by his daughter Libra and his son Adam. "My father was my best friend. I feel incredibly blessed to have been so deeply loved and to be his daughter. I hope that alongside his remarkable artistic legacy, people will remember his kindness, his gentleness, and how much he genuinely cherished putting joy into the world," his daughter said in statement.

item.title: China's Huawei sets 2027 launch for new AI chips as it targets Nvidia
item.description: Huawei Technologies (HWT.UL) will launch two new artificial-intelligence semiconductors in 2027, rotating chairman David Wang said on Thursday, as the Chinese tech giant builds up its AI computing business and seeks to challenge U.S. chipmaker Nvidia .
item.dc:creator: Che Pan, Casey Hall, Eduardo Baptista
item.content:encoded: Huawei Technologies (HWT.UL) will launch two new artificial-intelligence semiconductors in 2027, rotating chairman David Wang said on Thursday, as the Chinese tech giant builds up its AI computing business and seeks to challenge U.S. chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA.O) . Huawei plans to launch the 960DT in the first quarter of 2027 and the Ascend 960PR in the third quarter, Wang said. The company is also working on ways to connect very large numbers of AI chips, allowing them to work together as one bigger computing system. Most advanced AI programmes require more processing power than a single chip can provide. Wang said in a speech at a company even in Shanghai that Huawei's UnifiedBus technology would be a key link in the company's next generation of large AI systems. The technology is intended to help chips share information and work together more efficiently. Huawei has developed 11 semiconductors based on UnifiedBus technology for use in its large systems, Wang said. Its largest linked systems, which the company calls superclusters, can support up to 1 million AI processors, he added. Huawei has shipped more than 1,000 smaller linked systems, called supernodes, to more than 370 customers, Wang said. A supernode is a system that brings together many AI chips to tackle the same task. Wang did not say how many chips could be connected within a single supernode, name customers, or give a breakdown of shipments. HUAWEI PART OF CHINA'S AI PUSH The United States and China are competing to develop the chips, data centres and software that underpin artificial intelligence. Washington has imposed export controls that restrict China's access to certain advanced computing chips and semiconductor manufacturing equipment, while Chinese companies and policymakers have placed greater emphasis on building domestic alternatives. That has made the ability to connect chips increasingly important for Chinese technology companies. If they cannot freely buy the most advanced foreign chips, they can seek more computing power by joining larger numbers of locally available chips in one system. But that approach only works well if the chips can exchange information quickly enough. U.S. export controls have helped Huawei emerge as a prominent Chinese supplier of AI chips. Still, it faces a well-established market leader in Nvidia, whose hardware and software tools are widely used by developers around the world. A strong developer base will be important to Huawei's effort to make its hardware easier to use. Wang said Huawei's AI chip ecosystem had 5,270 monthly active developers.

item.title: Indian shares seen opening flat after Fed signals more hikes; NSE IPO in focus
item.description: Indian shares are set for a muted start on Thursday after the U.S. Federal Reserve raised interest rates and signalled further hikes, while elevated crude prices and a busy primary market led by the National Stock Exchange of India's IPO opening are expected to weigh on sentiment.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indian shares are set for a muted start on Thursday after the U.S. Federal Reserve raised interest rates and signalled further hikes, while elevated crude prices and a busy primary market led by the National Stock Exchange of India's IPO opening are expected to weigh on sentiment. GIFT Nifty futures were trading around 23,224.5 points, as of 7:58 a.m. IST, indicating a flat start for the Nifty 50 index, which closed at 23,217.60 on Wednesday. The Fed [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"raised"] rates by 25 basis points in a unanimous decision, its first increase in more than three years. Updated quarterly [USN:L6N45816B TEXT:"projections"] showed that 16 of 18 policymakers expected at least one additional 25-basis-point increase by year-end. Higher U.S. interest rates reduce the appeal of emerging markets such as India for global investors. They may also pressure sectors including information technology, where companies derive a significant portion of revenue from the United States. Brent crude eased slightly to about $106 a barrel after reports that Saudi Arabia had [USN:L4N45805M TEXT:"offered"] additional cargoes through Oman, easing some concerns over supply disruptions. However, restrictions around the Strait of Hormuz and persistent geopolitical risks continue to cloud the oil market outlook. Investors will also watch the NSE (NSEI.NS) IPO, which opens on Thursday and becomes the fifth active offering in the primary market. The exchange [USN:L4N4580ZT TEXT:"allocated"] shares worth 67.46 billion rupees ($703.07 million) to anchor investors on Wednesday, including Norway's and Abu Dhabi's sovereign wealth funds, at 1,785 rupees apiece, the upper end of the IPO price band. "With the IPO pipeline so crowded, a substantial amount of liquidity is likely to be absorbed by the primary market," said Arun Kejriwal, founder of Kejriwal Research and Investment Services. "Investor attention is overwhelmingly focused on new issues, leaving the secondary cash market relatively neglected."
